diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a constant $\zeta > 0$ such that for every $z \in \cS$, one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion quantifies $\bar{c}(y,z)\le -\zeta$, meaning all $m$ components simultaneously. Its negation gives $\forall y\,\exists j(y,k)$ with $\bar{c}_{j(y,k)}(y,z^k)>-\zeta_k$, where the index depends on $y$. The proof incorrectly upgrades this to a single $j$ satisfying $\bar{c}_j(y,z^k)>-\zeta_k$ for every $y\in\mathcal{Y}$. The remaining argument (passing to the limit to get $\bar{c}_j(y,z)\ge0$ for all $y$, then using MFCQ and a directional derivative to contradict this) depends on this unjustified single-$j$ claim.

failure_location.quote: Then there exist a positive sequence $\{\zeta_k\}$, a sequence $\{z^k\} \subset \cS$, and some $j \in \{1,...,m\}$ such that $\lim_{k\to\infty }\zeta_k = 0$ and

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Work throughout with $g(y):=\max_j \bar{c}_j(y,z)$ instead of a single $\bar{c}_j$. From $\forall y: g(y)>-\zeta_k$ derive $\min_y g(y)\ge-\zeta_k$; pass to $z^k\to z$ to obtain $\min_y g(y)\ge0$ at the limit; note $g(z)=\max_j c_j(z)\le0$ forces $\max_j c_j(z)=0$; apply MFCQ to find a direction along which every active $\bar{c}_j$ becomes strictly negative, contradicting $\min_y g(y)\ge0$. The compactness/MFCQ/directional-derivative architecture is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform Slater property is unproven. Every result depending on the explicit multiplier bound (SCP convergence rate, iteration complexity, oracle complexity) is unreliable until the proof is repaired.
issues.title: Unjustified single-index extraction in proof of uniform Slater theorem
issues.why_classification: The wrong inference requires restructuring several proof lines to use $\max_j$ arguments, but the theorem is correct and the repair uses the same mathematical ideas without new proof architecture or loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The auxiliary function $\phi$ (and the Lagrangian $\widetilde{L}=\phi+\langle\lambda,\bar{c}\rangle$) is defined without $q(z)$, so the claim $z^{k+1}=\arg\min_z\widetilde{L}(z,\lambda^k)$ is false: the KKT stationarity condition \eqref{thm2_KKT_Stationary} involves $\partial q(z^{k+1})$. Moreover, the step bounding $\frac{L_k}{2}(\|\hat{y}^k-z^k\|^2-\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2)$ by $\frac{L_k}{2}\|\hat{y}^k-z^{k+1}\|^2$ is a false geometric inequality (it would require $\langle\hat{y}^k-z^{k+1},z^{k+1}-z^k\rangle\le0$, which does not hold in general).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include $q(z)$ in $\phi$ (so $\phi(z)=\langle\nabla g(z^k),z\rangle+\frac{L_k}{2}\|z-z^k\|^2+q(z)$), making $z^{k+1}=\arg\min\widetilde{L}(z,\lambda^k)$ valid by KKT. Replace the false inequality by $\frac{L_k}{2}(\|\hat{y}^k-z^k\|^2-\|z^{k+1}-z^k\|^2)\le\frac{\bar{L}}{2}D_\mathcal{Y}^2$ to obtain the stated bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the explicit $\ell_1$ multiplier bound is invalid. The stated bound is correct but unproven as written; every result that uses this bound is unreliable.
issues.title: Lagrangian omits q and false geometric inequality in multiplier bound proof
issues.why_classification: Both corrections are local and routine (fix a definition, use the diameter bound), preserving every substantive claim and guarantee with no new argument or reoptimization.
